title: Portable call shim for legacy SDKs and compact parameter payloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers and partner SDKs send a mix of legacy tool call payloads (snake_case keys, string-ified numbers, optional metadata fields) and modern structured call messages. The runtime currently rejects many of these with hard errors which breaks integrations and increases support burden. Goal: design and implement a lightweight, portable 'call shim' that sits between the API surface and the strict runtime validator. The shim should: 1) accept a compact, stable JSON call-spec that covers the common legacy shapes; 2) perform incremental/streaming-friendly validation so large parameter blobs (e.g., complex JSON objects, file manifests) can be validated as they arrive; 3) apply safe coercions (string->number, 'true'/'false'->boolean) and canonicalize key naming (snake_case <-> camelCase) with a configurable tolerance level; 4) emit structured warnings for recoverable issues and standardized error codes for unrecoverable validation failures; 5) expose opt-in strict mode to enforce original runtime contracts for customers that require it. This ticket covers the schema format, validation rules, error taxonomy, and runtime feature flagging; implementation and integration tests will be separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact call-spec JSON format (one-page reference) that covers: param name, canonical type, allowed coercions, required/optional, example canonicalization rules
Design a streaming validation API that can validate tokens/partial payloads and surface early warnings without blocking streaming responses
Produce an error code list and mapping table to existing runtime errors: ERR_PARAM_MISSING, ERR_COERCION_FAILED, ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH, ERR_EXTRA_FIELD_IGNORED, ERR_STREAM_TRUNCATED
Provide SDK compatibility rules: when to auto-coerce, when to return a warning, and how to opt into strict enforcement
Proposal reviewed and approved by runtime and SDK owners; PR checklist and rollout plan attached

notes: Design must avoid logging raw parameter values. Telemetry should emit only structured flags (e.g., 'coercion_applied') and counts. Consider opt-out for regulated customers via Private config.
rollout_plan: feature flag on ingest: 'portable_call_shim' -> enable 5% traffic in hosted -> monitor coercion/warning rates and error conversions for 72h -> 25% -> 100% if no regression. For Dedicated/Private, expose an admin toggle and migration guide.
test_plan: unit tests for coercion rules, end-to-end tests with streamed payloads (simulate truncation + partial validation), backward-compat tests using SDK sample payloads (python/ruby/go), QA smoke with canary on runtime-1.20 cluster
